question: A can do a work in 9 days and B can do the same work in 19 days. If they work on it together for 6 days, then what fraction of the work is left?
solution:
**Given:**

A can complete the work in 9 days.

B can complete the work in 19 days.

They work together for 6 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work done in 1 day by A = 1 / time taken by A.

Work done in 1 day by B = 1 / time taken by B.

Total work done together in 1 day = Work done by A in 1 day + Work done by B in 1 day.

Work done together in 'n' days = Total work done together in 1 day × n.

Fraction of work left = 1 - Total work done together in 'n' days.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Work done in 1 day by A = 1 / 9.

⇒ Work done in 1 day by B = 1 / 19.

⇒ Total work done together in 1 day = (1 / 9) + (1 / 19).

⇒ Total work done together in 1 day = (19 + 9) / (9 × 19).

⇒ Total work done together in 1 day = 28 / 171.

⇒ Work done together in 6 days = (28 / 171) × 6.

⇒ Work done together in 6 days = 168 / 171.

⇒ Fraction of work left = 1 - (168 / 171).

⇒ Fraction of work left = (171 / 171) - (168 / 171).

⇒ Fraction of work left = 3 / 171.

⇒ Fraction of work left = 1 / 57.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/57.**
